label: LOC Ceasefire Violations (2026 YTD)
contestNote: Pakistan violated ceasefire for 10+ consecutive days in early May 2026 — most intense LoC breakdown since the 2021 DGMO ceasefire agreement. No new LoC incidents reported May 10–24; ceasefire holds at Day 379 on May 24.
deltaNote: Ceasefire broken July 17-19, 2026: first major LoC firing since Operation Sindoor truce, in the Tarkundi (Rajouri) and Balakote (Poonch) sectors — 435 days of calm ended. No casualties. Separately, a July 31 terror attack killed two non-local labourers at Kulgam, the first civilian attack in the Valley since Pahalgam. NIA chargesheeted 2 men (Aug 7-8) over a Pakistan-handled plot to bomb a passenger train and stage attacks in Punjab/Delhi. Pakistan's drawn-out AJK Assembly election concluded Aug 15 with PML-N winning 25 seats to PPP's 12, after weeks of deadly JAAC reserved-seat protests JKHRO says have killed at least 89 people since June. India called the polls a 'farce' (Aug 7); Pakistan rejected the criticism. On Aug 5 (Youm-e-Istehsal), Sharif and Dar called Article 370's revocation illegal; India's MEA rebutted that Pakistan has 'no locus standi.' On Aug 7, Pakistan signed the Mecca Joint Defence Agreement with Saudi Arabia and Turkey; India's MEA said Aug 11 it is 'examining implications' for national security. India's IB warned Aug 11 of an ISI-backed terror plot targeting J&K ahead of Aug 15 Independence Day, which passed off peacefully under heavy security. On Aug 14, PM Sharif called 'every single drop' of Pakistan's water a red line and threatened a 'direct' response over the IWT; India's MEA said Aug 14 there is 'no change' in its abeyance stance. Diplomatic sparring continued through the week: Pakistan quietly removed parking poles/barricades outside the Indian High Commission in Islamabad (~Aug 17); Pakistan extended its airspace ban on Indian aircraft to Sept 24 (Aug 19, 16th consecutive NOTAM extension); US Ambassador Sergio Gor called J&K 'an important part of India' during his first Srinagar visit (Aug 19), prompting Pakistan to summon the US Chargé d'Affaires and lodge a strong demarche; India reciprocated Pakistan's Islamabad move by demolishing unauthorised structures outside the Pakistan High Commission in Delhi (Aug 20). Amit Shah announced Aug 17 the bust of the ISI-backed 'Shahzad Bhatti Network' — 200+ arrests across 14 states, IEDs and Pakistan Ordnance Factory-marked grenades seized — which Pakistan's FO rejected Aug 18 as a 'malicious campaign,' countering with 'state-sponsored terrorism' accusations against India (citing the Kulbhushan Jadhav case). India's MEA dismissed Pakistan's protest over Ambassador Gor's remarks Aug 21, calling Delhi's barricade removal 'proportionate action' and reaffirming J&K as 'integral and indivisible.' AJK's 12th Legislative Assembly was sworn in Aug 24 after a final reserved-seat polling round; PML-N swept the Aug 25 speaker/deputy speaker elections (Chaudhry Tariq Farooq and Ahmed Raza Qadri, both 32-13 over PPP). The AJK premiership process then hit intra-party turbulence: Nawaz Sharif dropped his original nominee, AJK PML-N President Shah Ghulam Qadir, in favour of Barrister Iftikhar Gilani on Aug 27, prompting Qadir and ex-AJK PM Raja Farooq Haider to publicly withhold support; Qadir said he would boycott the Aug 28 assembly session and invoked Sharif's own 'Vote Ko Izzat Do' slogan. The Aug 28 assembly session to elect Gilani as 17th AJK PM proceeded on schedule (nominations 9:30am, vote 2pm, oath 4pm) despite the revolt, with PML-N's 32-seat coalition against PPP's 14 sufficient to seat him; voting in seven Poonch/Sudhnoti constituencies remains unfinished. Separately, NIA's Pahalgam probe (Aug 25) alleges a unified ISI command structure coordinating LeT/JeM/Hizbul in J&K with BKI/KZF in Punjab via Telegram-based radicalisation, building on the Aug 24 Chandigarh BKI IED-plot bust (3 arrested, ~5-6kg explosives seized). Gilani was formally elected 30-14 over PPP's Sardar Mukhtar Khan and sworn in as AJK's 17th PM on Aug 28. LoC activity ticked up overnight Aug 27-28: three suspected Pakistani drones crossed into Rajouri's Nowshera sector (Rumlidhara), Army fire forced them to retreat, and a separate suspected infiltrator was fired on and is believed still hiding as a large search operation continues; a second drone was tracked over Poonch's Mendhar sector (Behrooti village) the evening of Aug 28 before returning to Pakistan, with a search operation underway into Aug 29. Separately Aug 28, two hand grenades were recovered from a fleeing suspect during naka checking in Baramulla's Kunzer. None of these incidents produced casualties, but together they mark the most active 48-hour stretch of LoC drone/infiltration activity since the Jul 17-19 firing cluster. Bilateral freeze remains comprehensive: no ambassadors, $0 formal trade, IWT in abeyance; Pakistan on Aug 29 urged India to resume IWT technical dialogue and data-sharing, which India continues to link to Pakistan credibly ending cross-border terrorism support. Pakistan pressed its IWT internationalisation push through Aug 27-29: DPM/FM Ishaq Dar raised the treaty with UK Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband on Aug 27, and Pakistan's Ambassador to the US Rizwan Saeed Sheikh wrote Aug 28 that 'the IWT contains no provision allowing either party unilaterally to suspend it,' rebutting Indian Ambassador Vinay Kwatra. No new LoC incidents, casualties, or diplomatic escalations were reported Aug 30, though 25 Pakistani nationals (including fishermen) released from Indian jails crossed back via Wagah-Attari on Aug 29, reported Aug 30. On Aug 31, the Permanent Court of Arbitration issued its merits award on the Indus Waters Treaty, ruling the treaty 'remains fully in force' and barring further concreting at the Ratle hydro project pending a neutral expert's 2027 ruling; India's MEA flatly rejected the award as issued by a body with 'no jurisdiction whatsoever,' while Pakistan's FO welcomed it. Separately Aug 31, security forces busted a suspected militant hideout in Shopian's Naikpora Memender, recovering an AK-47, a pistol, a grenade and ammunition; no arrests reported. Pakistan's FO spokesperson Tahir Andrabi said Sep 2 Pakistan remains committed to the IWT 'in letter and spirit' and urged India to reciprocate; the same day, rival National Conference and BJP camps staged simultaneous gheraos in Srinagar and Jammu over J&K statehood and governance. On Sep 3, BSF apprehended Pakistani national Nazir Sadhir after he inadvertently crossed the IB near Kanachak, Jammu, repatriating him via Golpattan by Sep 7. A joint Army-Police-CRPF operation (Operation Ashdar) killed Pakistani LeT operative Yasir in Budgam's Ashdar Gali/Yousmarg area Sep 4, with his identity confirmed Sep 5; a search for at least one more suspected terrorist continued. At the SCO summit in Bishkek Sep 1, PM Modi called for 'no place for double standards' on terrorism in a veiled message to Pakistan; Pakistan marked its 61st Defence Day Sep 6 invoking last year's four-day conflict. On Sep 4-7, India and Pakistan sparred anew after a UN 'Correct the Map' cartographic-proportions resolution passed Sep 4: India's MEA said Sep 6 that J&K and Ladakh 'must be depicted in accordance with India's official map,' and Pakistan's FO rejected this Sep 7 as 'baseless assertions' contrary to J&K's internationally recognized disputed status. Pakistan's FO spokesperson Sajjad Haider Khan reiterated the same rejection Sep 8, saying India's 'so-called official maps and unilateral claims of sovereignty have no bearing on the status of the disputed territory' — no new substantive development beyond the Sep 7 position. Review of Sep 5, 8 and 9 found no new bilateral military or diplomatic incidents; the LoC itself has seen no new firing or infiltration incidents since the Aug 27-29 drone cluster; ceasefire holds at Day 487 on Sep 9. An IANS wire report Sep 10 cited anonymous Intelligence Bureau officials warning Pakistan's military, under pressure from ongoing PoK unrest (JAAC-led strikes paralysing Rawalakot, Bhimber, Mirpur, Neelum Valley and Muzaffarabad) and Balochistan violence, could attempt a 'misadventure' along the LoC — a skirmish or infiltration push — to divert attention; Indian agencies were said to be on high alert as a result. Separately Sep 10, satellite-imagery reporting (Indian Defence News, unconfirmed) described expanded Pakistani electronic-warfare infrastructure at Dadyal, PoK (~33 km from the LoC) and PAF Base Sindhri, Sindh. Neither claim reflects a confirmed LoC incident; no firing, infiltration or other event was reported Sep 10-11, and the ceasefire holds at Day 489 on Sep 11.
